entries.name: MCP server core (in-process agent control plane)
entries.purpose: createMcpServer() assembles ~107 MCP tools (counted by countUniqueMcpTools across routing/quota/budget/resilience/cache/compression plus memory, skill, agent-skill, github-skill, plugin, pool, gamification, notion, obsidian and local-corpus families) over the official SDK. Collision: these tools hand an MCP client management-plane write primitives (omniroute_switch_combo, set_budget_guard, set_routing_strategy, set_resilience_profile) that duplicate KK3's orchestration authority and Carol's catalog governance, so the HX lane keeps the surface disabled by default (mcpEnabled:false, settings.ts:172).
entries.risk_class: critical — full management-plane control exposed to any connected MCP client when enabled
dependencies: the Next.js app or CLI mcp-server entry
entries.test_contract: Enable in a lab setting, connect a client, assert tool list matches scope map; negative: mcpEnabled=false yields 503 at the HTTP transports.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Set settings.mcpEnabled=false (default) — stream/sse routes return 503 via guardEnabled (src/app/api/mcp/stream/route.ts:18-23); stdio launcher simply is not configured.

entries.name: MCP HTTP transports (streamable-HTTP + SSE)
entries.purpose: guardEnabled() 503s unless settings.mcpEnabled and the transport string matches, and every verb passes requireManagementAuth with the mcp:connect scope carve-out; the whole /api/mcp/ prefix is a Tier-1 LOCAL_ONLY entry (routeGuard.ts:34). Collision: the transport decision controls whether any off-box agent can reach the MCP control plane at all — the LOCAL_ONLY tier is the quarantine that keeps it on-LAN.
entries.risk_class: high — remote reachability of the MCP control plane if the guard tiers were relaxed
entries.test_contract: With MCP enabled and transport set, POST a JSON-RPC initialize over loopback and over LAN; negative: non-local peer denied by the LOCAL_ONLY tier before auth.
entries.rollback_or_disable: mcpEnabled=false or mcpTransport!='streamable-http'/'sse' returns 503/400; LOCAL_ONLY prefix match denies non-local peers unconditionally (routeGuard.ts:33-34).

entries.name: MCP stdio transport via CLI launcher
entries.purpose: startMcpStdio() serves the same MCP tool set over StdioServerTransport when an MCP client spawns the OmniRoute CLI entry (bin/mcp-server.mjs resolves dist or ts server, wired from bin/omniroute.mjs:304); per httpAuthContext.ts:51 stdio has no per-caller identity and stays on the env scope fallback. Collision: any local agent process that can run the CLI obtains the control plane with no caller attribution — an attribution gap KK3's work-order model does not have.
entries.risk_class: high — no per-caller identity on stdio; scopes fall back to process env
dependencies: a local MCP client configured to spawn the CLI
entries.test_contract: Launch the CLI mcp-server entry with a scoped env; assert tools callable; negative: with OMNIROUTE_MCP_ENFORCE_SCOPES=true and empty OMNIROUTE_MCP_SCOPES, tool calls are rejected as missing_scopes.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Do not configure the MCP client (inert by default — no listener exists); when launched, OMNIROUTE_MCP_ENFORCE_SCOPES=true plus a minimal OMNIROUTE_MCP_SCOPES set constrains it.

entries.name: MCP per-tool scope enforcement
entries.purpose: evaluateToolScopes checks each tool's required scopes from MCP_TOOL_MAP against caller scopes resolved authInfo→meta→env, with wildcard support and fail-closed tool_definition_missing; enforcement runs only when OMNIROUTE_MCP_ENFORCE_SCOPES==='true' (server.ts:104) — otherwise every caller is allowed (scopeEnforcement.ts:107-109); resolveMcpCallerAuthInfo binds real per-key api_keys.scopes on HTTP/SSE and fails closed to the fallback chain. Collision: this is OmniRoute's own delegation-to-agents authorization model, parallel to KK3's work-order scoping — two authority models for the same plane.
entries.risk_class: medium — enforcement is env-gated and fail-open by default; per-key binding exists on HTTP transports
entries.test_contract: With enforcement on, call a write:combos tool with a read-only key and assert missing_scopes; with enforcement off, confirm the documented allow-all path (lab evidence for the owner).
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unset OMNIROUTE_MCP_ENFORCE_SCOPES (default) removes enforcement; full quarantine remains mcpEnabled=false.

entries.name: MCP tool-call audit trail
entries.purpose: logToolCall persists hashed inputs and summarized outputs to a dedicated mcp_tool_audit SQLite table (better-sqlite3 with node:sqlite fallback), queryable via management-gated /api/mcp/audit(+stats). Collision: none — this is the observability counterpart the owner authority plane needs if MCP is ever enabled; it records, it does not control.
entries.risk_class: low — append-only audit store; no control authority
entries.test_contract: Enable MCP in lab, fire one tool call, assert one audit row with hashed input; persistence: restart and re-query.
entries.rollback_or_disable: No writes occur while the MCP server is disabled; table can be left in place (append-only evidence).

entries.name: MCP introspection routes (tools catalog, status)
entries.purpose: GET routes expose the MCP tool catalog and runtime status to management callers, accepting the mcp:connect scope; read-only introspection used by the dashboard Endpoints page. Collision: minor — read-only; the mcp:connect scope is the same carve-out the transports use, so its bypass policy (localOnlyManageScopeBypassEnabled default true, settings.ts:228-229) governs reach.
entries.risk_class: low — read-only introspection
entries.test_contract: GET both routes with a manage-scope token; negative: without auth expect 401/403 per the central pipeline.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Central MANAGEMENT classification plus requireManagementAuth gates; no separate disable needed.

entries.name: A2A JSON-RPC endpoint (/a2a)
entries.purpose: The /a2a router serves A2A v0.3 methods (message/send, message/stream, tasks/get, tasks/cancel) plus v1.0 aliases (SendMessage/SendStreamingMessage, route.ts:31-34), and rejectIfA2ADisabled returns JSON-RPC -32000/503 unless settings.a2aEnabled===true (default false, settings.ts:173). Collision: this endpoint lets OmniRoute act as an agent peer accepting task delegation from foreign agents — the exact inverse of KK3's sole-orchestrator rule, hence disabled by default and owner-gated.
entries.risk_class: high — inbound task delegation channel from arbitrary A2A clients when enabled
entries.test_contract: Enable in lab, run message/send against a builtin skill and a v1.0 alias; negative: disabled state returns error code -32000 with HTTP 503.
entries.rollback_or_disable: settings.a2aEnabled=false (default) — every method short-circuits at rejectIfA2ADisabled.

entries.name: A2A task manager (lifecycle state machine)
entries.purpose: A2ATaskManager runs submitted→working→completed|failed|cancelled transitions with UUID ids, in-memory storage with optional SQLite persistence, 5-minute default TTL, a concurrent-task limit, and GHSA-jcm5 owner scoping (sha256 of the API key; ownerless keyless tasks stay visible to every caller by design, taskManager.ts:49-54). Collision: durable task state inside the gateway is orchestration state — if A2A is ever enabled, KK3 must treat this store as subordinate state, never truth.
entries.risk_class: medium — in-memory task state with a keyless-visible ownership carve-out
entries.test_contract: Drive a task through every legal transition; negative: illegal transition rejected; persistence: enable SQLite backing and restart to confirm reload.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Only reachable when a2aEnabled; clearing in-memory state is process restart; TTL expiry reaps stale tasks.

entries.name: A2A authentication posture (keyless local-first)
entries.purpose: authenticateA2ARequest mirrors the /v1 posture: REQUIRE_API_KEY on → valid OmniRoute key required; else OMNIROUTE_API_KEY env → timing-safe token match; else keyless allow (authenticate.ts:40-41), with resolveA2AOwner hashing the key for task scoping; the REST task routes independently re-check a2aEnabled!==true (tasks/route.ts:119). Collision: under the local-first keyless default any LAN peer could drive agent tasks the moment the feature flag flips — the flag and the key posture are separate axes the owner must set together.
entries.risk_class: medium — keyless-by-default auth mirrors /v1; exposure only materializes when A2A is enabled
entries.test_contract: With A2A enabled: no key → 401 when REQUIRE_API_KEY=true; wrong key rejected via timing-safe compare; keyless mode allowed and ownerless tasks listed.
entries.rollback_or_disable: a2aEnabled=false closes the surface regardless of key posture.

entries.name: A2A agent card discovery (/.well-known/agent.json)
entries.purpose: The well-known route always serves an A2A v0.3 agent card (name, url, capabilities, skills) merged with Conductor fleet skills when the hub is reachable; PACKAGE_VERSION falls back to the stale literal '1.8.1' (route.ts:17) when npm_package_version is unset [UPSTREAM drift — package is 3.8.51]; the status route only embeds the card when A2A is enabled. Collision: the card advertises OmniRoute-as-agent to any discovering orchestrator — marketing the control plane KK3 does not want advertised; centrally MANAGEMENT-classified (non-/api path falls to the fail-closed default).
entries.risk_class: low — read-only advertisement, but it publishes capability metadata (and a stale version fallback) to any authenticated peer
entries.test_contract: GET the well-known route and the agent-card.json twin; assert the card validates; content check: version matches package.json when run under npm.
entries.rollback_or_disable: No per-route disable; the card is inert metadata while a2aEnabled=false (status route omits it).

entries.name: A2A built-in agent skills (6 handlers)
entries.purpose: A2A_SKILL_HANDLERS lazily imports six builtin skills (smart-routing, quota-management, provider-discovery, cost-analysis, health-report, list-capabilities) that execute prompts through the OmniRoute pipeline and return routing_explanation/cost/resilience/policy metadata. Collision: these are agent-callable macros over the routing plane — foreign agents could steer routing analysis through A2A tasks; subordinate to the same a2aEnabled gate.
entries.risk_class: medium — agent-invokable analytics over the routing plane
entries.test_contract: With A2A enabled, execute each builtin skill once and validate artifact shapes; negative: unknown skill id rejected.
entries.rollback_or_disable: a2aEnabled=false disables the whole handler path; no per-skill flags exist.

entries.name: ACP CLI-agent registry (host CLI detection)
entries.purpose: detectInstalledAgents probes the host for codex/claude/gemini/goose (+operator-defined custom) agent CLIs by execFileSync'ing their version commands (registry.ts:13, definitions at :53); POST accepts client-chosen custom binaries persisted to settings; the routeGuard comments classify /api/acp/agents as an RCE-via-tunnel spawn surface and gate it LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:72). Collision: the registry exists so OmniRoute can discover and drive host agent CLIs — an orchestration-adjacent capability that steps on KK3's commissioning authority; the LOCAL_ONLY tier is the quarantine.
entries.risk_class: high — version-probe spawns plus client-defined binary registration (loopback-constrained)
entries.test_contract: GET the route from loopback and assert detection shape; negative: non-loopback peer denied by the LOCAL_ONLY tier; register a custom agent then remove it.
entries.rollback_or_disable: LOCAL_ONLY tier blocks remote callers; deleting settings.customAgents removes custom entries; no global enable flag exists because detection is on-demand only.

entries.name: ACP process spawner (CLI-as-backend transport)
entries.purpose: AcpManager.spawn launches a registered CLI agent as a child process with piped stdio, shell:false, and the FULL OmniRoute process env merged under caller-supplied env (manager.ts:65-69) — Coder-X corroborated the unfiltered env inheritance: provider credentials present in the gateway env flow into agent children; hasRegisteredAgent is the only quarantine (:54), and no production call site outside src/lib/acp references AcpManager (grep-verified — currently unwired). Collision: OmniRoute spawning agent processes is precisely the process-spawning class the HX disabled-by-default rule freezes, and 'CLI-as-backend' makes the gateway an agent runtime competing with KK3's execution substrate.
entries.risk_class: critical — child processes inherit gateway env secrets; arbitrary registered binaries
entries.test_contract: Static: assert no route wiring reaches spawn (grep); dynamic lab: register a benign CLI, spawn, assert env allowlisting requirement before any HX use.
entries.rollback_or_disable: No runtime wiring exists today (inert); if ever wired, the registry whitelist plus the LOCAL_ONLY API tier are the quarantine; removing custom agents closes the binary set.

entries.name: Memory engine (per-key long-term memory store)
entries.purpose: The memory engine provides CRUD over typed memory rows (api-key-scoped, session-optional, TTL/expiry, TV6 typed-decay columns) with a 60s/500-entry cache; getMemorySettings defaults enabled:false (settings.ts:33,101) and the REST API is management-gated. Collision: a second long-term memory living inside the traffic gateway competes with Carol's catalog/second-brain governance (who owns remembered knowledge, provenance, expiry) — the HX lane keeps it disabled by default.
entries.risk_class: high — persistent per-key memory that silently shapes future prompts if enabled
entries.test_contract: Disabled: retrieve returns empty and injection is skipped; enabled lab: create/retrieve/expire a memory and assert api-key scoping isolation between two keys.
entries.rollback_or_disable: memoryEnabled=false (default) disables retrieval, injection, and the reindex path; rows persist but stay unread — delete via the management API for full quarantine.

entries.name: Memory+skills injection into the chat traffic path
entries.purpose: injectMemoryAndSkills runs on every chat request: it retrieves owner memories (memorySkillsInjection.ts:116) and injects them plus enabled skill tools into the outbound body; the per-request x-omniroute-no-memory:true header nulls the owner and disables both branches (chatCore.ts:1248-1252). Collision: silent prompt mutation inside the traffic plane — invisible to clients unless they send the opt-out header — is an observability and owner-authority concern even when memory itself is approved.
entries.risk_class: high — in-path request mutation; default-on once memoryEnabled
entries.test_contract: With memory enabled, assert an injected block appears and that the opt-out header removes it; negative: memoryEnabled=false injects nothing.
entries.rollback_or_disable: memoryEnabled=false globally; per-request x-omniroute-no-memory:true header (always available).

entries.name: Memory vector backends (sqlite / Qdrant / Obsidian)
entries.purpose: Memory backends are pluggable behind the MemoryBackend interface: local SQLite vectors (default), an external Qdrant cluster (host/port/apiKey/collection/quantization config, qdrant.ts:16-26), and an Obsidian backend that reads/writes memories as Markdown+frontmatter files in a user vault path (obsidianBackend.ts:2-29). Collision: Qdrant moves governed memory content to an external service (egress + retention outside the plane) and Obsidian writes into arbitrary user filesystem locations — both need an owner decision on data placement; backend selection lives in memory settings and all backends die with memoryEnabled=false.
entries.risk_class: medium — external/filesystem data placement of memory content
entries.test_contract: Lab: point at a throwaway Qdrant collection and a temp vault dir, assert round-trip; negative: unreachable Qdrant degrades per backend health check.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Backend selection reverts to sqlite; memoryEnabled=false disables all backends; no external target is contacted while disabled.

entries.name: Embeddings backing service (memory + /v1/embeddings)
entries.purpose: createEmbeddingResponse routes embedding requests through the provider/combo machinery (embeddingRegistry, familyGuard dimension checks) and treats private/LAN hosts as trusted no-auth per the #6925 comment (service.ts:39-40) with outbound URL guard imports for cloud targets. Collision: minor — it is traffic-plane, but it is also the memory pipeline's embedding source, so memory enablement inherits its LAN trust posture; no orchestration content.
entries.risk_class: medium — LAN no-auth trust class for the embeddings route feeds the memory pipeline
dependencies: provider or combo with an embedding model
entries.test_contract: Direct: POST /v1/embeddings against a configured provider; negative: unknown embedding provider yields the formatted error; persistence: none.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Traffic-plane standard path; removing embedding providers/combos disables it; memoryEnabled=false removes the memory consumer.

entries.name: Skill registry + executor
entries.purpose: SkillExecutor.execute blocks only when settings.skillsEnabled === false (executor.ts:43-46) — getSettings carries NO hardcoded skillsEnabled default (grep-verified across src/lib/db), so an unpersisted key means execution is allowed; executions are audited into skill_executions rows (:64-75) and skills are stored per api-key with enabled/mode flags (registry.ts:119-130). Collision: user-defined executable capabilities inside the gateway bypass KK3's work-order scoping, and the default-allow gate means the disabled-by-default rule is NOT enforced by the code for this surface — an owner-set skillsEnabled=false row is required to actually disable it.
entries.risk_class: high — default-allow execution gate contradicts the HX disabled-by-default rule until explicitly set
entries.test_contract: Unset key: execute a builtin skill via /api/skills/executions and record that it runs (evidence of default-allow); set skillsEnabled=false and assert the 403-style error; per-skill enabled=false rejects by name.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Persist settings.skillsEnabled=false (explicit — the code default is allow); per-skill enabled=false in the registry; management API is requireManagementAuth-gated.

entries.name: Skill tool injection + interception in provider requests
entries.purpose: Enabled skills are advertised to models as provider-native tools (name@version, base64url-encoded under the omr_skill_ prefix when needed, injection.ts:33-41) and their calls are intercepted and executed gateway-side with builtin aliasing (web_search/web_fetch fallbacks, interception.ts:31-34); customSkillExecutionEnabled===false blocks custom-skill interception (:279). Collision: this gives models tool-level access to gateway-managed capabilities — agent-like autonomous behavior inside the traffic plane, gated only by the same default-allow skills posture (CAP-P7-018).
entries.risk_class: high — models gain executable tools mid-stream
entries.test_contract: With a test skill enabled, assert the tool appears in the outbound payload and its call is intercepted; negative: skillsEnabled=false strips injection (memorySkillsInjection both-branch disable).
entries.rollback_or_disable: skillsEnabled=false globally; per-skill enabled=false; builtinToolNames allowlist constrains builtins per request.

entries.name: Skill sandbox (container-runtime execution)
entries.purpose: SandboxRunner executes skill code in containers (docker/apple/wsl/orbstack/podman auto-detected, SKILLS_SANDBOX_RUNTIME override, containerProvider.ts:12-15) with defaults cpu 100 / mem 256MB / 30s timeout / network disabled / read-only fs (sandbox.ts:25-31); runtime detection probes binaries via spawnSync and fails closed when none exists (containerProvider.ts:71-79). Collision: container spawning on the host is the process-spawning class — on HX hosts container runtimes are rick's plane, so this stays lab-only; the isolation defaults are sound but the capability itself needs an owner decision.
entries.risk_class: high — host container execution; mitigated by network-off/read-only defaults and fail-closed runtime detection
dependencies: a container runtime on the host
entries.test_contract: Lab only: run a trivial image and assert network-isolation and read-only flags reach the runtime command; negative: no runtime installed → provider resolution fails, no spawn.
entries.rollback_or_disable: No container runtime on the host → hard fail-closed; SKILLS_SANDBOX_RUNTIME can pin or the sandbox caller path stays unused while skills are disabled.

entries.name: Built-in + memory-builtin skill handlers
entries.purpose: builtinSkills and memoryBuiltinHandlers provide the prepackaged handlers (web_search, web_fetch with pinned fetch-backend support, browser, and memory CRUD tools surfaced as model-callable tools, MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES at interception.ts:36) registered at startup with a chunk-singleton fallback. Collision: memory builtins give models direct write access to the memory store when memory is enabled — model-driven memory mutation crosses into Carol's knowledge-governance lane; otherwise standard capability code.
entries.risk_class: medium — model-invokable memory mutation among otherwise benign builtins
entries.test_contract: Execute each builtin directly with a test input; negative: builtin not in the request allowlist is not resolved (interception.ts:44-49).
entries.rollback_or_disable: Same gates as CAP-P7-018/019; memory builtins additionally die with memoryEnabled=false.

entries.name: skills.sh external skill provider install
entries.purpose: The skillssh install route fetches third-party SKILL.md content via fetchSkillMd and registers it globally, but only when the active skills provider setting is 'skillssh' (409 otherwise, route.ts:23-32); authenticated via isAuthenticated. Collision: importing unvetted external skill definitions is a supply-chain path into the skill registry (and from there into model tool lists) — owner approval and content provenance review belong before any use.
entries.risk_class: high — third-party content supply chain into executable skills
entries.test_contract: With provider=skillssh, install a known test skill and assert registry row + provenance fields; negative: provider unset returns 409.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Provider setting not switched (default path rejects with 409); uninstall removes the registry row.

entries.name: GitHub skill collector (external repo discovery + install)
entries.purpose: githubCollector searches GitHub for SKILL.md-bearing repos, scores them, scans for blocked patterns (malware/secrets), and installs skill files INTO EXTERNAL AGENT DIRECTORIES (Hermes, Claude, etc. per the module header, githubCollector.ts:1-11). Collision: it reaches out to GitHub (egress) and writes into other agents' host directories — crossing the owner authority plane and other lanes' filesystems; the blocked-pattern scan is the only quarantine besides not calling it.
entries.risk_class: high — writes to foreign agent directories plus GitHub egress
dependencies: target agent directories on the host
entries.test_contract: Dry-run a search and inspect scoring; negative: a repo matching blocked patterns is refused; never run install outside a lab directory.
entries.rollback_or_disable: On-demand API only (no scheduler found); skipping use leaves nothing running; installed files are plain files removable by hand.

entries.name: Skill Collector CLI detection + chaos dispatch
entries.purpose: The /api/skills/collect/ tree probes the host for installed CLI tools via child-process detection — classified RCE-via-tunnel and gated LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:69) — while the single chaos dispatch route is PUBLIC-by-exact-path but enforces its own Bearer validateApiKey check (chaos/route.ts:67) per the publicApiRoutes.ts:54-60 contract. Collision: host probing plus an externally-triggerable dispatch endpoint into skill execution — the LOCAL_ONLY tier covers the probes; chaos mode is the one intentionally-public hole and needs its flag+key evidence before any owner sign-off.
entries.risk_class: high — host CLI probing; one public exact route with per-handler auth
dependencies: chaos mode flag for the chaos route
entries.test_contract: GET detect from loopback (shape check) and from LAN (expect LOCAL_ONLY denial); POST chaos without a key (expect 401) and with a key when enabled.
entries.rollback_or_disable: LOCAL_ONLY tier for /api/skills/collect/; chaos requires its own enabled flag plus a valid key — both absent by default.

entries.name: Agent-skills catalog + skills/ SKILL.md corpus
entries.purpose: 45 generated SKILL.md manifests (23 API + CLI families per skills/README.md and the generator header 'all 45 agent skills', generator.ts:2) teach any external agent (Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, Cline, Continue) how to drive OmniRoute's management API — keys, settings, backups, tunnels, MCP — and are served read-only via GET /api/agent-skills (no route-level auth; central MANAGEMENT classification applies). Collision: this corpus advertises the full management-plane control surface to arbitrary agents — a competing catalog to Carol's curated knowledge governance, publishing exactly the capabilities the HX lane keeps disabled.
entries.risk_class: medium — read-only, but it is a public advertisement of the entire control surface to any agent that can read it
entries.test_contract: GET /api/agent-skills and count entries vs the skills/ tree; content check: omni-mcp advertises 107 tools/32 scopes vs the measured scope list (17 MCP scopes — drift worth recording).
entries.rollback_or_disable: Read-only catalog; removing the skills/ tree or the route removes the advertisement; nothing executes from these files server-side.

entries.name: Agent-skills SKILL.md generator (build tooling)
entries.purpose: generateAgentSkills rebuilds SKILL.md files from the OpenAPI spec and CLI registry with a hard safety contract — dryRun=true default, writes require dryRun=false, deletion requires prune AND dryRun=false (generator.ts:10-15) — and the generate route is management-gated. Collision: none material — doc synthesis tooling; its output feeds CAP-P7-025's advertisement concern.
entries.risk_class: low — filesystem writes possible only under explicit non-default flags
entries.test_contract: Run generator default (assert zero writes and a dry-run report); lab: dryRun=false against a temp copy and diff.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Default dry-run; generated files are overwritable artifacts (regeneration is the inverse).

entries.name: Plugin manager (install/activate lifecycle)
entries.purpose: The plugin manager coordinates scanner, loader, DB rows, and hook registry for install/activate/deactivate/uninstall, with assertWithinPluginDir (manager.ts:77-81) blocking rm of any path outside the plugin root even from a tampered DB pluginDir; the API tree is LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:56-57) as a child_process code-exec class. Collision: third-party code lifecycle inside the gateway — the plugin class is named in the charter's disabled-by-default list; nothing ships installed (scanner reads ~/.omniroute/plugins which is operator-populated).
entries.risk_class: high — third-party code lifecycle management inside the gateway process
entries.test_contract: Scan an empty plugin dir (zero plugins, no errors); lab: install a fixture plugin, activate, assert DB status transitions; negative: tampered pluginDir delete attempt throws.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Deactivate+uninstall via the API (path-guarded rm); LOCAL_ONLY tier blocks remote lifecycle calls; empty plugin dir means nothing loads at boot.

entries.name: Plugin loader (child-process isolation + env filtering)
entries.purpose: loadPlugin runs each plugin in a separate node child process over IPC (spawn process.execPath with a temp host script, stdio ignore/pipe/pipe/ipc, loader.ts:198-206) with a permission-filtered environment (getFilteredEnv allowlists safe keys unless the 'env' permission widens it, :386-395), SRI-format integrity hashing (:37-40), 10s hook timeout and SIGKILL grace. Collision: this is the gateway's third-party code execution engine — process-spawning class; the env filter is the only runtime permission enforcement found (see CAP-P7-903), so declared network/file/exec permissions are not code-enforced here.
entries.risk_class: critical — executes third-party code on the host; isolation is process-level only, permission enforcement partial
entries.test_contract: Load a fixture plugin and assert IPC ready/result round-trip; inspect the child env for allowlisted keys only; negative: hook timeout yields SIGTERM→SIGKILL cleanup.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Deactivate the plugin (child is killed, temp host script removed); no plugins loaded while none installed.

entries.name: Plugin manifest + permission schema
entries.purpose: plugin.json is validated against a manifest schema whose requires.permissions enum is network|file-read|file-write|env|exec (manifest.ts:11), defaulting to an empty permission list (:123), and the granted set is persisted to the DB at install/scan. Collision: the schema is the dashboard-visible contract for plugin authority — but enforcement beyond env filtering was not found (CAP-P7-903), so the declaration currently outruns the mechanism; owner review must treat manifests as claims, not guarantees.
entries.risk_class: medium — permission declarations without full runtime enforcement
entries.test_contract: Validate manifests missing/extra fields against the schema; assert DB row records the declared permission set at install.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Schema-level only; uninstalling plugins removes the rows.

entries.name: Plugin marketplace (remote registry install)
entries.purpose: The marketplace browses and installs plugins from a registry URL guarded by isSafeMarketplaceUrl — http(s) only, literal-private rejection, and A+AAAA DNS resolution with any-private-address rejection failing closed (marketplace.ts:35-60) — plus safeOutboundFetch public-only with redirect blocking for the fetch itself. Collision: remote code supply chain into the gateway (Phase 1 local seed registry, Phase 2 remote per the header) — the SSRF posture is strong, the supply-chain decision is the owner's.
entries.risk_class: critical — downloads and activates third-party code from a remote registry
entries.test_contract: Point at a lab registry fixture, install, assert integrity + manifest validation; negative: registry hostname resolving to a private IP is rejected (A and AAAA cases).
entries.rollback_or_disable: Do not configure/use the marketplace (inert by default); installed plugins uninstall through the path-guarded manager.

entries.name: Plugin hooks + fs-watch hot reload
entries.purpose: Plugins register lifecycle hooks (onRequest/onResponse/onError/onInstall/onActivate/onDeactivate/onUninstall, manager.ts:31-40) that run in the request path, and a directory watcher auto-reloads changed plugin dirs after a 500ms debounce (watcher.ts:4,36-47). Collision: in-path request/response mutation by third-party code, plus filesystem-triggered code reload — a tampered plugin file becomes live code without any management action; the watcher means 'disabled by default' must include not watching empty dirs.
entries.risk_class: critical — unvetted code mutating traffic plus fs-triggered reload
entries.test_contract: Activate a fixture hook plugin and assert onRequest fires in order; touch a plugin file and observe debounced reload; negative: deactivated plugin emits no hooks.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Deactivation unregisters hooks (unregisterHooks) and stops watching; nothing watched while no plugins are installed.

entries.name: Pre-request middleware hooks (vm.Script compilation)
entries.purpose: The pre-request hook registry compiles operator-supplied JS into reusable vm.Script objects (registry.ts:111-118) that run in priority order BEFORE provider selection and can mutate body/headers, redirect to a different model/combo, or short-circuit a response (:7-13); the routeGuard classifies /api/middleware/ with the plugins code-exec tier and gates it LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:58). Collision: arbitrary code rewriting routing decisions in the hot path — an ungoverned second routing brain competing with KK3's route governance; Coder-X independently classed it as untrusted-code-execution authority.
entries.risk_class: critical — operator/supplied JS executes in the request hot path and can redirect traffic
entries.test_contract: Register a fixture hook that tags a header and assert order/effect; negative: compile error in hook code is rejected at registration; LAN peer denied by LOCAL_ONLY tier.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove hook configurations (registry initializes empty without them); LOCAL_ONLY API tier blocks remote hook management.

entries.name: Eval framework (builtin + custom suites)
entries.purpose: The eval runner executes builtin suites (golden/coding/reasoning/multilingual/safety/instruction/codex-comparison, evalRunner.ts:14-22) and custom DB suites against live models by POSTing through the local chat-completions route (runtime.ts:1-5) and persisting runs; strategies exact/contains/regex (safe-regex)/custom; the API is management-gated. Collision: none with KK3 — evaluation is owner-evidence machinery — but runs burn provider quota and touch real models, so it stays operator-triggered lab work.
entries.risk_class: low — read/evaluate-only; cost side effects on providers
entries.test_contract: Run a tiny builtin suite against a lab combo and assert persisted run rows; negative: unknown suite id 404s.
entries.rollback_or_disable: No background scheduler found — nothing runs unless invoked; deleting runs/suites is plain CRUD.

entries.name: Router-eval observation records
entries.purpose: routerEval defines typed RouterObservation records (sampleId, routeInput, configId, selected vs expected model, latencyMs, costUsd, success) with an input-normalization parser for offline router-quality evaluation. Collision: none — pure data-shaping for evaluation evidence; supports the owner's routing-correctness questions without touching traffic.
entries.risk_class: low — type/parsing utilities only
entries.test_contract: Feed malformed and well-formed observation inputs and assert normalization outcomes (unit-level).
entries.rollback_or_disable: Library only — nothing to disable.

entries.name: Model self-assessment loop (/api/assess)
entries.purpose: POST /api/assess fans an assessment run across every auto/* model via loopback /v1 calls (assessor.ts:57) and categorizes fitness with a SelfHealer; the route carries NO route-level auth and relies on the central MANAGEMENT fallback (classify.ts:122-126); its self-auth env var is misspelled OMNIROUTe_API_KEY at both use sites (route.ts:15,147) so the intended key never resolves and it silently falls back to API_KEY/empty [FACT — code bug/drift]. Collision: a one-POST fleet-wide probe storm burning quota on every model is an orchestration-grade action with a broken credential knob — owner evidence required before any use, and the typo belongs in the drift register.
entries.risk_class: medium — unauthenticated-at-route bulk model probing; broken env-var spelling defeats its own configuration
entries.test_contract: Confirm centrally-gated 401 without management auth; lab: POST with scope model and assert exactly one model probed; record the typo fallback behavior as evidence.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Central MANAGEMENT classification is the gate; not calling it leaves nothing running; results are in-memory in the Assessor instance.

entries.name: Cloudflare tunnel (cloudflared binary lifecycle)
entries.purpose: The cloudflared module downloads the binary from the GitHub releases API (cloudflaredTunnel.ts:13-14, sha256-pinned asset specs) and spawns it to publish OmniRoute at a public URL, with persisted tunnel state; the API is authenticated and the POST lifecycle is LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:43). Collision: any tunnel publishes the entire gateway (management plane included) beyond the 192.168.50.0/24 LAN — the owner rule reserves boundary widening to an owner decision, so this surface is BLOCKED for HX use regardless of its internal guards.
entries.risk_class: critical — public internet exposure of the whole service; binary supply chain
dependencies: network egress to GitHub + Cloudflare edge
entries.test_contract: Static review only for HX: verify the download pins sha256 and the spawn is LOCAL_ONLY-gated (done, this ledger); no live enablement without an owner decision.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Not installed/not started by default; stop path exists in the module; removing the managed binary dir completes quarantine.

entries.name: Tailscale Serve/Funnel tunnel
entries.purpose: The tailscale module drives tailscaled/login/serve/funnel subprocesses (funnel result typing at tailscaleTunnel.ts:64-65) via enableTailscaleTunnel (enable/route.ts:15) with tailscaleEnabled defaulting false (settings.ts:146); every mutation endpoint (enable/disable/install/login/start-daemon) is individually LOCAL_ONLY-listed (routeGuard.ts:44-48). Collision: tailnet-only Serve stays near the HX boundary model, but Funnel is public-internet exposure identical in class to cloudflared — owner decision required; the per-endpoint LOCAL_ONLY listing is the quarantine that already exists.
entries.risk_class: critical — Funnel publishes the service publicly; daemon lifecycle spawns system services
entries.test_contract: Static review for HX (done); lab-only: enable serve (not funnel) on a throwaway tailnet and assert URL shape; negative: non-local peer denied on every mutation route.
entries.rollback_or_disable: tailscaleEnabled=false default; disable route stops funnel/serve; uninstall path removes the daemon integration.

entries.name: ngrok tunnel
entries.purpose: The ngrok module starts a listener targeting http://127.0.0.1:<apiPort> (ngrokTunnel.ts:30-33) and reports a public URL whose /v1 becomes the published API URL (:35-37); the route is authenticated via isAuthenticated. Collision: identical exposure-boundary class as the other tunnels — a one-call public URL for the whole gateway conflicts with the HX LAN boundary rule absent an owner decision.
entries.risk_class: critical — public internet exposure of the whole service
entries.test_contract: Static review for HX (done); no live enablement planned without owner approval.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Not started by default; stop the listener via the module; no persisted state beyond the listener global.

entries.name: Webhook dispatcher (HMAC-signed event egress)
entries.purpose: deliverWebhook POSTs HMAC-SHA256-signed (sha256= prefix, dispatcher.ts:20-22) event payloads to registered URLs with a 10s timeout and up to 3 retries, re-validating the URL against the outbound SSRF policy at dispatch time (:45,:78); the hot-path wrapper is fire-and-forget over dispatchEvent (:132-141) with deliveries recorded for history. Collision: an automated egress channel carrying request/quota metadata off-box — controlled entirely by who may register webhooks (management API) and by the URL guard; no orchestration content, but it is a data-exfiltration-shaped surface the owner should see in the boundary review.
entries.risk_class: medium — outbound event egress; SSRF-guarded at create and dispatch; no durable retry queue (CAP-P7-902)
entries.test_contract: Register a lab webhook to a local listener, fire test.ping, assert signature header format and delivery row; negative: private/LAN URL rejected at create and at dispatch.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Delete the webhook rows — no registrations, no dispatches; dispatcher has no standalone process.

entries.name: Webhook management API + chat integrations
entries.purpose: The management API CRUDs webhooks of kinds slack/telegram/discord/custom (route.ts:19) over events request.completed/request.failed/quota.exceeded/test.ping plus wildcard (eventDescriptions.ts:1), validating non-telegram URLs with parseAndValidateWebhookUrl inside a zod superRefine (:31-40); telegram kind uses the Bot API instead of a raw URL. Collision: chat-ops integrations as a notification plane — benign, but telegram's guard exemption means its egress path (Bot API token) needs the same secret-handling review as any credential.
entries.risk_class: medium — management CRUD with per-kind egress transformers
entries.test_contract: Create/update/test/delete each kind in lab; negative: private URL rejected with the zod issue message; telegram kind skips URL validation by design (assert it).
entries.rollback_or_disable: requireManagementAuth gates every verb; deleting webhooks disables all egress.

entries.name: Embedded service supervisor (child-process lifecycle)
entries.purpose: ServiceSupervisor is the generic supervisor for embedded services (9router, CLIProxyAPI, future per its header): spawn with ignore/pipe/pipe stdio and detached:false (:27-44), ring-buffered logs, health probes that flip the service to error after consecutive failures, and a registry that stops all supervisors on SIGINT/SIGTERM (registry.ts:20-42); the /api/services/ tree is LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:42). Collision: daemon lifecycle management inside the gateway is the process-spawning class — supervised daemons also become nested providers (CAP-P7-043), compounding the traffic-plane risk.
entries.risk_class: high — long-lived child daemons supervised in-process
entries.test_contract: Start a fixture service in lab and assert state transitions + log ring; kill -9 the child and assert error surfacing; negative: non-local API caller denied.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Stop via the supervisor (SIGTERM path) or the stop route; registry stopAll runs on shutdown; LOCAL_ONLY tier blocks remote control.

entries.name: Embedded service installers (npm/binary supply chain)
entries.purpose: Installers pull third-party daemons into DATA_DIR: 9router via npm view/install (ninerouter.ts:7-8,:50) using an execFile-only npm wrapper (utils.ts:5), plus cliproxyapi, dario, bifrost, and mux — whose own header calls it 'a local agent-orchestration daemon' (mux.ts:4). Collision: installing mux literally installs a competing orchestrator inside the HX factory — the sharpest control-plane collision in this partition (KK3 is the sole orchestrator); the whole family is also a remote supply chain into supervised processes, so it stays disabled pending per-service owner review.
entries.risk_class: critical — third-party daemon supply chain; mux is an agent-orchestration daemon competing with KK3
entries.test_contract: Static inventory (done here); lab-only: install 9router into a temp DATA_DIR and assert execFile-only npm usage; never install mux outside an owner-approved experiment.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Not installed by default; uninstall removes the DATA_DIR service tree; supervisors stop before removal.

entries.name: Service backends registered as passthrough providers
entries.purpose: serviceBackends maps the supervised 9router/cliproxyapi daemons to provider-plugin manifest entries — OpenAI-format, no auth, passthroughModels:true, sidecar-ineligible as 'runtime provider' (serviceBackends.ts:3-6,18-38) — so a supervised daemon becomes a routable provider inside OmniRoute. Collision: OmniRoute routing into a nested router (9router is itself a routing daemon) delegates route decisions to a layer HX cannot see or verify — traffic-plane correctness risk on top of the process-spawning class.
entries.risk_class: high — unverifiable nested routing behind a passthrough provider entry
entries.test_contract: With a lab 9router running, route one request through the passthrough provider and compare against direct provider routing; negative: daemon down surfaces the supervisor error state, not silent fallback.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Removing the provider rows / stopping the service detaches the nested router; nothing registers while services are uninstalled.

entries.name: Restart/shutdown remote lifecycle endpoints
entries.purpose: POST /api/restart and /api/shutdown are management-authed one-liners that SIGTERM the gateway process after a 500ms reply delay (restart relies on an external process manager to come back). Collision: remote lifecycle control of the traffic plane — legitimately a management function, but no feature-flag disable exists for either route (CAP-P7-904), so management-token hygiene and the LOCAL_ONLY bypass policy are the only quarantines; availability impact makes it owner-visible.
entries.risk_class: high — remote process termination of the gateway
dependencies: an external process manager for restart to return
entries.test_contract: In lab, POST restart and assert SIGTERM + supervisor stopAll evidence; negative: unauthenticated POST rejected by requireManagementAuth.
entries.rollback_or_disable: None in source (no flag found — CAP-P7-904); restrict manage-scope tokens and keep the routes behind the central pipeline.

entries.name: Job registry + background scheduled services
entries.purpose: The JobRegistry lists cron/interval jobs (DTO-whitelisted, jobs/route.ts:17-31) with enable/disable/run-now child routes — the whole tree LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:64-65) — while boot wiring checks OMNIROUTE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_SERVICES with a truthy-set parser that defaults to RUNNING when unset (instrumentation-node.ts:105-109). Collision: unattended background work (backup schedules, cloud sync, proxy/health schedulers) is the workflow class the HX rule freezes; the env kill-switch exists but is default-off, so 'disabled by default' requires setting it explicitly at deployment.
entries.risk_class: medium — default-on background scheduling; kill-switch available
entries.test_contract: Boot with OMNIROUTE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_SERVICES=1 and assert no job registrations; default boot lists jobs via the LOCAL_ONLY API; run-now one job and inspect its run row.
entries.rollback_or_disable: OMNIROUTE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_SERVICES=1 at boot; per-job disable via the LOCAL_ONLY API.

entries.name: Telegram bot gateway (bot webhook + Mini App proxy)
entries.purpose: The telegram update route is PUBLIC-classified (publicApiRoutes.ts:25-29) and serves two callers: Telegram bot updates (503 when TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is unset — never a silent no-op, route.ts:11) and Mini App posts whose initData HMAC is verified before proxying chat through the OmniRoute pipeline. Collision: a public, dashboard-auth-free chat channel into the traffic plane — who may drive the gateway is an owner-authority question; the bot-token gate is the quarantine and it is default-closed.
entries.risk_class: high — public unauthenticated-to-dashboard ingress into chat completions when a bot token is configured
entries.test_contract: POST an update with no token configured (expect 503); with a lab token, assert /start and a proxied chat reply; negative: bad initData HMAC rejected.
entries.rollback_or_disable: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN unset (default) hard-closes the route with 503.

entries.name: Admin concurrency/semaphore inspection + reset
entries.purpose: GET /api/admin/concurrency reports rate-limit and account-semaphore stats and POST performs admin actions such as semaphore resetAll, all behind requireManagementAuth. Collision: minor — capacity control is P6's plane (ledgered there); this entry records only the admin endpoint's existence so the remote-administration surface is complete; no orchestration content.
entries.risk_class: low — operational inspection plus a reset mutation
entries.test_contract: GET and assert both stat blocks; lab: POST reset and assert semaphores clear; negative: unauthenticated rejected.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Management-auth gated; nothing to disable beyond token hygiene.

entries.name: Conductor hub integration (external OmniConductor orchestrator)
entries.purpose: hubProxy reads CONDUCTOR_HUB_URL/TOKEN (hubConfig returns null when unset, hubProxy.ts:84-87) and proxies Faro ask, fleet snapshots, and task detail with whitelisted shapes and server-side tokens; bridge.ts MIRRORS the external hub's SSE task events into the local A2A TaskManager with an explicit state mapping (bridge.ts:1-8). Collision: the most direct KK3 competitor found — an external orchestration plane driving OmniRoute-local task state and agent cards; Coder-X read it as 'client for an external orchestrator', which for the HX lane IS the collision [INFERENCE on severity, FACT on mechanism]; env-unset keeps it inert (degraded offline responses, never 5xx).
entries.risk_class: critical — external orchestration hub can drive local A2A task state and fleet advertising
entries.test_contract: Unset env: assert degraded offline shapes from fleet/ask; lab-only with a fixture hub: assert task events mirror into the A2A TaskManager per the state ladder.
entries.rollback_or_disable: CONDUCTOR_HUB_URL unset (default) — hubConfig null disables every interaction; no local state persists.

entries.name: Cloud agent providers (Jules/Devin/Codex-Cloud/Cursor-Cloud)
entries.purpose: The cloudAgent registry wires four REMOTE cloud coding agents as task targets — Jules (https://jules.googleapis.com/v1alpha, julesApi.ts:2), Devin, codex-cloud, and cursor-cloud (registry.ts:7-14) — reached via their REST APIs with API-key credentials. Collision: double — delegating work to cloud agents violates the HX local-model-first/no-cloud rule if ever used, and it hands agent execution authority to third-party clouds; inert until credentials are configured, but the HX disposition is BLOCKED regardless of mechanism quality.
entries.risk_class: critical — cloud egress plus agent-execution delegation to third parties
dependencies: cloud agent API credentials (unconfigured by default)
entries.test_contract: Static inventory only for HX (done); no live calls permitted under the no-cloud rule.
entries.rollback_or_disable: No credentials configured → no agent is callable; removing credential rows completes quarantine.

entries.name: Issue agent (recorded triage executor)
entries.purpose: The issue agent replays recorded triage runs through the local chat-completions pipeline with model/provider env overrides, a 60s default timeout capped at 120s (execution.ts:25-27,43-47), and a RecordedTriageTimeoutError; the routeGuard keeps /api/issue-agent/ LOCAL_ONLY 'until sandbox + audit hardening is complete' (routeGuard.ts:55). Collision: an agent-like autonomous triage loop — the disabled-by-default class; the upstream guard comment itself acknowledges the hardening gap, supporting a LAB-ONLY posture.
entries.risk_class: medium — bounded autonomous loop; upstream itself flags missing sandbox/audit hardening
entries.test_contract: Run a recorded fixture in lab and assert timeout enforcement; negative: >120s timeout requests clamp to the cap.
entries.rollback_or_disable: LOCAL_ONLY tier confines it; no scheduler or always-on trigger found.

entries.name: MITM agent bridge (host TLS interception)
entries.purpose: The MITM manager spawns server.cjs as a child process, provisions /etc/hosts DNS overrides (manager.ts:11 dns imports), and installs a system-wide trusted root CA via privileged steps (runPrivilegedMitmStep, :30; cert install :13) to intercept agent CLI traffic; after GHSA-x7vm-hp44-9p79 both /api/tools/agent-bridge/ and /api/settings/mitm are LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:51-53). Collision: host trust-store and DNS mutation is rick's OS lane and the owner's authority plane, not OmniRoute's — plus it turns the gateway into a TLS-interception appliance; BLOCKED for HX absent an explicit owner decision and rick's sign-off.
entries.risk_class: critical — system trust-store + DNS mutation and TLS interception of host processes
dependencies: root/sudo for CA install and hosts edits
entries.test_contract: Static review only for HX (done); the LOCAL_ONLY reclassification after the GHSA is verified here by reading the guard entries.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Not enabled by default; teardown paths exist (removeDNSEntries/stopDnsTeardown imports); never run the enable flow on an HX host.

entries.name: VNC browser-login sessions (containerized credential harvest)
entries.purpose: The VNC session service spawns Docker browser containers (service.ts:1) for provider web-login flows, waits for CDP, and harvests session state into provider credentials (harvest import :9), tracking labeled sessions with idle reaping (:42-45); the routeGuard gates /api/vnc-session/* LOCAL_ONLY as the GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj spawn class (routeGuard.ts:71). Collision: automated credential capture plus container spawning — secret-handling and owner-authority planes intersect; requires owner acceptance and a threat model before any HX use (critical change class).
entries.risk_class: critical — automated harvesting of provider session credentials via spawned browsers
entries.test_contract: Lab-only with a throwaway provider account: run a session, assert harvest writes only credential fields and the container is reaped; negative: non-local caller denied by the guard.
entries.rollback_or_disable: On-demand only (no sessions exist by default); LOCAL_ONLY tier; session teardown removes containers and profile dirs.

entries.name: Copilot LLM driver (tool-executing assistant surface)
entries.purpose: The copilot module defines tools letting an LLM 'configure OmniRoute on behalf of the user, query the codebase via CodeGraph, and execute CLI commands for full control' (tools.ts:1-5) via execFile/execSync (:7); the routeGuard describes /api/copilot/ as an 'unauthenticated LLM driver' kept CLI-only by default with an opt-in manage-scope bypass (routeGuard.ts:50). Collision: an LLM with CLI execution authority over the gateway is the strongest agent surface in the corpus — it converts model output directly into host commands; default loopback confinement is the only thing between it and remote abuse.
entries.risk_class: critical — LLM-driven CLI execution against the host/gateway
dependencies: an LLM backend for the copilot
entries.test_contract: Static review (done); lab-only: confirm the LOCAL_ONLY tier denies LAN callers and the bypass requires an explicit manage-scope grant.
entries.rollback_or_disable: LOCAL_ONLY default; the manage-scope bypass is opt-in with a global kill-switch (localOnlyManageScopeBypassEnabled).

entries.name: OAuth host-credential auto-import (Cursor/Kiro/Raycast)
entries.purpose: The oauth auto-import routes read HOST-LOCAL credential files (cursor binary probe, kiro-cli data, Raycast tokens) to import provider credentials; publicApiRoutes.ts:105-114 deliberately excludes them from the PUBLIC /api/oauth/ prefix so they fall to MANAGEMENT and reach the LOCAL_ONLY tier (routeGuard.ts:66-68) after GHSA-wgwc/gxv4. Collision: host credential access is the owner authority plane — the mechanism is correct (loopback-only) and ledgered here because it is an agent-adjacent host surface; provider credential lifecycle itself stays with P2/P4.
entries.risk_class: high — reads host-local credential material (loopback-confined)
dependencies: the respective CLIs installed on the host
entries.test_contract: From loopback with a fixture CLI config, import and assert credential fields land encrypted per the P5 path; negative: LAN caller denied by LOCAL_ONLY tier.
entries.rollback_or_disable: LOCAL_ONLY tier; not invoking the routes reads nothing.

entries.name: NOT-ESTABLISHED: true ACP wire-protocol implementation
entries.purpose: Searched src/lib/acp/** and src/app/api/acp/** for the Agent Client Protocol (session/initialize handshake, ACP-spec JSON-RPC method set): found only generic stdio piping described as 'JSON-RPC style' (manager.ts:5) and CLI detection — the name 'ACP' denotes a CLI-as-backend transport here, not the Zed/AionUi ACP specification [INFERENCE from absence; registry header cites AionUi auto-detection as the reference]. Collision: none beyond CAP-P7-012/013 — recorded so no one assumes spec conformance.
entries.risk_class: low — honest absence record
entries.test_contract: Re-grep for 'session/initialize' or acp-spec schemas when upstream claims ACP conformance.
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a — nothing found to disable.

entries.name: NOT-ESTABLISHED: durable webhook retry queue
entries.purpose: Searched webhookDispatcher.ts and the webhook db modules for a persistent delivery queue: dispatch is fire-and-forget (Promise.allSettled inside dispatchEvent, :132-141) with in-call retries only (maxRetries=3, deliverWebhook :71-76); delivery HISTORY is persisted (getDeliveries, deliveries/route.ts:8) but a crash between attempts loses pending retries — no queue table or scheduler found [INFERENCE from absence]. Collision: none; recorded as a resilience gap for the owner.

entries.test_contract: Kill the process mid-retry in lab and assert the pending delivery is lost (expected) — evidence for the gap.

entries.purpose: Searched loader/manager/hooks for code enforcing the manifest's network/file-read/file-write/exec permissions at runtime: the only enforcement found is environment-variable filtering (getFilteredEnv, loader.ts:386-395, fed from manifest permissions at :165); the child process keeps full network/fs/exec ability of the host user [INFERENCE from absence]. Collision: the manifest schema (CAP-P7-029) advertises guarantees the runtime does not provide — owner must treat plugin permissions as documentation until enforcement exists.

entries.test_contract: Lab: a network-less-declared fixture plugin attempts an outbound fetch and succeeds (expected) — proving the gap.

entries.purpose: Searched the feature-flag registry and both lifecycle routes for a disable switch: the routes mount unconditionally with requireManagementAuth as the only gate [INFERENCE from absence]. Collision: availability-affecting remote admin without an off switch — recorded so the owner can request one or accept the risk.
entries.risk_class: low — management-auth compensates; no flag exists

entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a — nothing found to disable.

entries.purpose: Searched all three tunnel modules for path/scope restriction of the published URL: ngrok targets the service root (ngrokTunnel.ts:30-33) and cloudflared/tailscale show no path filtering in the regions read — tunnels publish the WHOLE gateway (dashboard + management API + /v1), not just the client API [INFERENCE from absence]. Collision: strengthens CAP-P7-036/037/038's BLOCKED disposition — even an approved tunnel would expose the management plane.
entries.risk_class: medium — whole-surface publication when any tunnel runs
entries.test_contract: If a tunnel is ever owner-approved, verify from outside that /api/<management> is reachable (expected: yes — the gap).

entries.purpose: Searched src/lib/acp/** for resource limits, sandboxing, or env allowlisting around spawned agent processes: spawn uses piped stdio with the full gateway env merged under caller env (manager.ts:65-69) and nothing else [INFERENCE from absence]; contrast with the skill sandbox's network-off/read-only defaults (sandbox.ts:25-31) which ACP does not reuse. Collision: raises CAP-P7-013's effective risk — agent children would run with gateway secrets and no containment.
